fact_en:
Why is the queen ant so much bigger?

A queen ant is usually bigger than the workers, especially her belly, which is full of eggs. Her chest is also larger because that's where her wings used to attach.
fact_bis:
Ngano nga mas dako ang reyna kaysa mga trabahante nga langgam?

Ang reyna kasagaran mas dako kaysa mga trabahante, ilabi na ang iyang tiyan nga puno sa itlog. Mas dako sab ang iyang dughan kay didto kaniadto nakakabit ang iyang mga pako.

findings.note: Queen ANT card turned into a bird card and never corrected. bis: "Ngano nga mas dako ang reyna kaysa mga trabahante nga LANGGAM?" and title_bis "Reyna sa Langgam" (= Queen of the Birds) for title_en "The Bigger Queen Ant". In Cebuano langgam = bird (hulmigas/subay/hantik = ant); the word 'ant' appears nowhere in the Cebuano, and the wing detail ("didto kaniadto nakakabit ang iyang mga pako") makes the bird reading fully coherent, so a child reads a false fact about birds. Tagalog-interference (Tg langgam = ant).

fact_en:
Why do ants walk in a line?

Ants walk one behind another because the leaders leave a scent trail on the ground that the rest follow straight to the food.
fact_bis:
Ngano sunod-sunod molakaw ang mga subay?

Ang mga subay molakaw nga sunod-sunod tungod kay ang nag-una magbilin og baho sa yuta nga sundon sa mosunod paingon sa pagkaon.

findings.note: title_bis "Langgam sa Linya" = "Birds in a Line" for title_en "Ants Follow Scent Lines". The body is correct ("ang mga subay molakaw nga sunod-sunod..."), but the displayed title names a different animal than the card, mirroring the known iro/cat title defect; same ant->langgam slip also at ffct-00110 and ffct-01426.

fact_en: Fiber from veggies and fruit isn't digested, but it helps your large intestine push waste along and keeps constipation away.
fact_bis: Dili matunaw sa lawas ang fiber gikan sa gulay ug prutas, apan motabang kini sa dakong bituka aron molihok ang basura ug malikayan ang tibi.

findings.note: Dietary-fiber card ends "malikayan ang tibi". In Cebuano `tibi` is the everyday word for TB (tuberculosis); constipation is Tagalog `tibi`. A Cebuano-only reader gets the false health claim "fiber prevents TB", and nothing in the card restores "hard stool / constipation" — the surrounding text only says fiber helps the large intestine move waste. The corpus's other constipation card (ffct-10342) keeps the English word "constipation" in the Cebuano, so this rendering is unique to this card (one grep hit corpus-wide, so low blast radius).

fact_en:
Where did all your body's cells come from?

Every one of the trillions of cells in a baby's body came from just one single first cell!
fact_bis:
Asa naggikan ang tanan nimong selula?

Ang tanan sa binilyon nga selula sa lawas sa bata naggikan sa usa ra ka unang selula!

findings.note: EN says the body's cells number in the trillions; bis says "ang tanan sa binilyon nga selula" = billions, a 1000x understatement of the number. The card contradicts itself: title_bis is "Trilyon Selusa Usa" while the body says binilyon, so a child reading only the Cebuano gets two conflicting magnitudes and the stated number in the body text is simply wrong. Should be "trilyon".

fact_en: The Tubbataha Reefs in Palawan are home to a rich variety of sea life — including giant clams that filter seawater to get their nutrients.
fact_bis: Ang Tubbataha Reefs sa Palawan puy-anan sa daghang linalang sa dagat, lakip ang dagkong tahong nga nag-filter-feed aron makakuha og nutrisyon gikan sa dagat.

findings.note: "giant clams" rendered `tahong` in both title_bis ("Tubbataha Gigante nga Tahong") and body ("dagkong tahong"). `Tahong` is the green mussel, a different bivalve; the giant clam is `taklobo` in Cebuano — and card ffct-14477 in this same batch uses `taklobo` correctly. Nothing in the card corrects it, so the child learns Tubbataha is known for giant mussels rather than giant clams.

fact_en:
How do ants share food with each other?

A worker ant doesn't eat everything itself — it passes food mouth-to-mouth to another ant, so the whole colony gets fed!
fact_bis:
Giunsa pag-ambit sa pagkaon sa mga langgam?

Dili ubuson sa worker ant ang tanang pagkaon — iluwa niini ang bahin gikan sa baba ngadto sa baba sa laing langgam, aron makakaon ang tibuok kolonya!

findings.note: Ants card: the Cebuano question and body use `langgam`, which is BIRD in Cebuano (Tagalog interference — Tagalog langgam = ant). Q: `Giunsa pag-ambit sa pagkaon sa mga langgam?` and `...baba ngadto sa baba sa laing langgam`. A Cebuano child reads a card about birds sharing food mouth-to-mouth in a colony; the body never corrects it (only the title `Hulmigas` and the untranslated English `worker ant` hint at ants). Sibling card ffct-14661 uses `hulmigas` correctly, confirming the corpus norm.

fact_en:
Why is the sailfin lizard protected?

Its home is being destroyed and people catch it to sell as a pet — so Philippine law now bans catching or selling this lizard.
fact_bis:
Ngano protektado ang sailfin lizard?

Gina-guba ang iyang puy-anan ug gidakop kini para ibaligya isip binuhi — mao nga bawal na kini dakpon o baligyaon sa balaod sa Pilipinas.

findings.note: title_bis 'Tiki nga Layag' names the sailfin lizard a tiki (house gecko) — a different animal. The Cebuano body never corrects it: it keeps the English 'sailfin lizard' and gives no Cebuano name, and the card's own terms list carries the correct 'ibid'. A child reading only the Cebuano learns that the protected animal is a house gecko.

fact_en: After the germ used in a vaccine is grown, it gets purified, measured into correct doses, and filled into clean vials before being shipped to clinics.
fact_bis: Human matubo ang mikrobyo nga gamiton sa bakuna, limpyohan kini, sukdon sa saktong dosis, ug ibutang sa limpyo nga botelya sa dili pa ipadala sa mga klinika.

findings.note: title_bis "Pangandoy sa Bakuna" for "Making Vaccines": pangandoy = a wish/aspiration/dream, not making or producing (paghimo). The body describes the manufacturing steps but never uses paghimo/produksyon, so the headline names a different thing and the card never corrects it.

fact_en:
How are evaporation and condensation related?

They are opposites! Heat causes evaporation, while cooling causes condensation.
fact_bis:
Unsaon pagkaugnay ang pag-alisngaw ug pamuo?

Magkasukwahi sila! Ang kainit maoy hinungdan sa pag-alisngaw, ug ang kabugnaw maoy hinungdan sa pamuo.

findings.note: title_bis "Alisngaw ug Paghalay" for "Evap vs Condensation": paghalay is hanging laundry out to dry, not condensation. The headline pairs evaporation with hanging-out-washing, and the body never links paghalay to anything — it calls condensation "pamuo" — so the wrong term in the headline is never corrected. A child scanning titles (and this corpus has neighbouring cards about clothes drying, e.g. ffct-14952/ffct-14960) is led to read condensation as drying laundry, i.e. the reverse of the process the card teaches.

fact_en: Plastic doesn't rot easily! That means it stays in our environment for a super long time.
fact_bis: Dili dali madunot ang plastik! Mao nga magpabilin kini sa atong kinaiyahan og dugay kaayo.

findings.note: title_bis "Plastic dili Mabuak" = "plastic does not BREAK", but the card (title_en "Plastic Doesn't Rot", body "Dili dali madunot ang plastik") is about not ROTTING. The body never mentions breaking, so the headline's claim is never corrected — and it is false: plastic does break (ffct-15081/15082 in this same batch say plastic breaks into microplastics). Correct title word is "madunot".

fact_en:
Does invisible air have weight?

Yes! Even though we cannot see it, a gas like air still has weight.
fact_bis:
Naa ba gabat ang dili makitang hangin?

Oo! Bisan dili nato kini makita, ang gas sama sa hangin naa gihapoy gabat.

findings.note: Card's whole point is "air/gas has weight", but the Cebuano never uses a Cebuano word for weight. Body: "Naa ba gabat ang dili makitang hangin? ... ang gas sama sa hangin naa gihapoy gabat" — `gabat` is Bikol (magabat), not Cebuano (bug-at / gibug-aton / timbang), and it is a HAPAX in the whole 47k-card corpus (1 hit, this card). title_bis "Bigat Hangin" is Tagalog `bigat`, so the title does not restore it either. A child reading only the Cebuano gets "invisible air still has [unknown thing]" and cannot state that air has weight. Moderate confidence on the lexical call; the hapax count is what pushed it over the line (grep is safe — the pattern hits only this card).

fact_en:
Where does our firewood come from?

Firewood used as fuel comes from the branches and trunks of trees!
fact_bis:
Asalinhagikan ang atong kahoy nga sugnod?

Ang kahoy nga sugnod naggikan sa mga sanga ug lawas sa mga kahoy!

findings.note: Body question is corrupted: "Asalinhagikan ang atong kahoy nga sugnod?" — a merged non-word where "Asa gikan..." belongs. The prompt a child is asked to answer is unreadable Cebuano (the answer sentence is fine). Not dialect variation, a text corruption.
